$comment: The Lane-A engine pin — the EXACT published bce-engine version that gates this tree independently of the code under review. See docs/pin-ceremony.md and docs/self-hosting.md §'Lane A / Lane B'. Bumping this pin is a PR gated by the OLD pin (a trust-anchor ratchet), never an in-line edit.
rangeRationale: EXACT pin only — never ^0.1.0, ~0.1.0, or @latest. Lane A must be independent of the code under review, so it installs a fixed published artifact. A range would let a later publish silently change the grader every contributor is measured against, reintroducing the trusting-trust hole Lane A exists to close. The caret-0.x incident is the recorded reason: on a 0.x line `^0.6.0` is equivalent to `~0.6.0` and EXCLUDES 0.7.0, so a caret pin does not even receive a minor bump — it ships dead-green.
publishedNote: true as of the 0.1.0 publish to the public npm registry. Lane A is ACTIVE: self-gate.yml installs the pinned published engine and grades this tree with an artifact it did not build. Flipping this to true BEFORE `npm publish` succeeds would arm a REQUIRED check against a version npm cannot serve, wedging every PR — publish first, verify `npm view bce-engine version` returns 0.1.0, then land this.
trustAnchor: The pinned engine is the PUBLISHED artifact from the public registry, so a defective change to the engine in a PR under review cannot influence the Lane-A verdict — Lane A rebuilds nothing from the branch.
